page: Microsoft Azure E128-64as_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance running on Microsoft Hyper-V. It features a constrained-core configuration designed for high-memory footprints relative to processing capacity. Powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9V45 processor clocked at 4.5 GHz, the instance provides 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 32 physical cores with 2 threads per core. Each physical core has access to 48 KB of L1 data cache and 1.0 MB of L2 cache, supported by a 32 MB L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX, AVX-512 (with VNNI and BF16 support), AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

The primary resource focus of the instance is its massive memory capacity. It is equipped with 1024.0 GB of RAM, resulting in a high ratio of 16.0 GB per vCPU. Benchmark results reflect this design: PassMark memory testing ranks in the top 10% with a score of 2981.55, and memory bandwidth reaches 203.18 GB/sec read and 133.05 GB/sec write on 256MB uncached blocks. Single-core processing is similarly robust, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2882.0 and stress-ng single-core performance of 3612.96, both landing in the top 10% tier. Multi-core Geekbench performance achieves 26844.0, while PassMark database operations record 36965.7.

Hardware tradeoffs are evident in storage and accelerator support. The E128-64as_v7 includes no local storage and no GPUs, requiring network-attached storage architectures for persistence. Cost efficiency is optimized for software licensing models that charge per vCPU while demanding vast memory tables. With half the vCPUs of a full 128-vCPU instance profile yet preserving the full 1024 GB RAM footprint, it offers an economical compute-to-memory structure for licensed enterprise software. This configuration aligns directly with in-memory caching platforms such as Redis, large-scale relational databases, and enterprise data processing tasks.
